# **Businesses today are in constant evolution.** 

**Reimagining how they build, reducing impact while staying efficient. Designing experiences that feel seamless, personal and consistent at every touchpoint.** 

**And extending care beyond boundaries, using data to deliver better outcomes, everywhere.** 



### **Together, limitless**<sup>**TM**</sup> 

### **Different industries. Different journeys.** 

**Different priorities.** Yet all are moving towards the same need to stay connected across systems, respond in real time, and make decisions with clarity. 

In today’s world, progress is no longer defined by what one company can achieve alone. 

‘Together, limitless<sup>TM</sup> ’ is a statement of intent. It reflects Tata Communications’ belief that meaningful progress is unlocked through deep collaboration across customers, partners and teams, unbounded by geography, scale or convention. 

In a world where technology is advancing at extraordinary speed, enterprises are navigating an ever-deepening layer of complexity legacy systems, fragmented data, expanding platforms, and rising expectations for seamless, omni-channel experiences. At the same time, the stakes are higher than ever, with growing demands for speed, resilience, security and trust. Managing this complexity while staying futureready is the defining reality of modern business. 

Our relevance has grown alongside our customers’ ambitions. This promise reflects our ability to evolve at speed, shaping ourselves around our customers’ business outcomes, as they transform. 

At its core, it defines how we show up, bringing together our platforms, expertise and people with our customers’ vision, and working side by side to overcome complexity with clarity and purpose. Because in a landscape often defined by noise, what enterprises seek most is integration, trust, and a partner who can help them move forward with confidence. 

This is where Tata Communications’ digital fabric comes in. It simplifies complexity by orchestrating cloud, edge, network and security into one cohesive, intelligent ecosystem. 

More than connectivity, it enables transformation. By unifying disparate systems into an integrated architecture, it enhances visibility, simplifies management, and creates a secure, scalable foundation for hyperconnected operations that helps organisations move faster, innovate smarter, and operate with confidence. 

The next five years will shape the next fifty. As AI, cloud and edge converge in unprecedented ways, enterprises will need ecosystems that can adapt, scale and evolve in real time. Positioned at this intersection, Tata Communications is building for what comes next - where technologies align, innovation accelerates, and possibilities expand. 

By enabling real-time, always-on, anywhere operations and unlocking the power of integrated data and intelligence, we help businesses move with clarity and confidence. 

Because when systems work as one, complexity fades and when ambition is supported by the right foundation – possibilities become limitless.

## **<u>About the Report</u>** 

### Our Approach 

Our Integrated Annual Report, aligned with the International Integrated Reporting Council ('IIRC'), sums up our financial as well as non-financial performance during the year, and informs all our stakeholders about our governance practices, material issues, risks, opportunities, strategy and prospects. 

Integrated thinking shapes how we design strategy, allocate capital and measure performance. We prioritise matters that are material to our business and stakeholders, aligning them with long-term growth, risk management and responsible governance. By linking financial outcomes with environmental, social and operational performance, we ensure that decision-making remains disciplined, forward-looking and resilient in a rapidly evolving digital ecosystem. 

Through this Report we are sharing Tata Communications’ vision for digital transformation, aligning with our overarching purpose, strategy and business model. We are providing here a transparent overview of how we create value for our stakeholders across the short, medium and long-term through the Company’s financial, environmental and societal activities. 

### Value creation through integrated thinking 

### Reporting Period 

Our approach shapes how we respond to: y Material matters impacting enterprise value y Short, medium and long-term performance priorities y Capital allocation and risk management y Sustainability imperatives 

This Report is published for the 12-month period from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026. Where relevant, comparative data from earlier periods has been included to provide a contextual perspective. 

Stakeholder engagement is embedded within the value creation process, ensuring that our use of and impact on the capitals remains balanced, accountable and aligned with long-term strategic objectives. 

### Reporting scope and boundaries 

This Report covers Tata Communications’ global operations and includes relevant information on our subsidiaries, associates and key operating geographies where it is material to our performance and value-creation narrative. Any exclusions or boundary limitations are disclosed in the relevant sections. 

### Feedback 

We welcome feedback and dialogue with our stakeholders. For general comments: <u>investor.relations@tatacommunications.com</u> For ESG-specific queries: <u>EOHS@tatacommunications.com</u> 

### Reporting frameworks and principles 

This Integrated Annual Report has been prepared in accordance with the guiding principles and content elements of the IIRC Framework. Disclosures within this Report are mapped, where applicable, to the Global Reporting Initiative (‘GRI’) Standards. The financial and statutory sections of the Report comply with the following: (a)The Companies Act, 2013, (b) Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), (c) SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, (d) Secretarial Standards issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India.

## **Because the Next Phase is Integrated** 

Businesses today do not just need connectivity. They need a simple way to bring together their people, applications, data and customers across many systems. This is where the shift from fiber to fabric becomes important. Fiber built the foundation. Fabric brings everything together into a single, integrated layer, where network, cloud, interaction and intelligence capabilities work together, enabling enterprises to operate seamlessly, respond faster to change and scale with greater efficiency. 

## **Built on Reach** 

Tata Communications is built on a strong connectivity heritage that has enabled us to reach and connect enterprises across geographies. For years, this infrastructure helped our customers move data, run operations and stay connected in an increasingly borderless world. But as enterprises became more digital, their needs changed. **Enterprises no longer wanted just connectivity; they demanded intelligent, agile, secure digital infrastructure.**

## **Strength to Scale. Scale to Grow** 

**The Power of Becoming** 

As customer needs became more complex, we expanded our role. We were no longer only carrying enterprise traffic. We were helping customers in navigating changes across cloud, cybersecurity, IoT, media, mobility, and customer-interaction platforms. Capability investments and acquisitions, such as The Switch<sup>TM</sup> and Kaleyra<sup>TM</sup> helped us deepen our digital portfolio and move closer to the business needs of global enterprises. 

# Together, **limitless** 

We mark the next step in our evolution as a leading global communications technology player. Our refreshed corporate identity and global positioning signal a more unified and future-focused direction, built to strengthen our competitive edge in an increasingly digital and interconnected world. 

Our journey has moved through two clear phases. In the first phase, we became financially fit. We built a more disciplined balance sheet and strengthened the business from within. In the second phase, we used that strength to invest organically and inorganically in capabilities that could shape our digital fabric. We are now entering the next phase, where the priority is profitable growth built on relevance, scale and deeper customer adoption. 

At its core, the refreshed brand identity is based on a clear belief: greater possibilities emerge when technology platforms, expertise and partnerships come together. As enterprises look for speed, security, resilience and accountability, our role is to help them operate with greater confidence and move beyond conventional boundaries. We are bringing capabilities, customers and partners together to enable enterprise growth without boundaries.

# **Letter from the Chairman** 

## **Balancing Resilience with Ambition** 

**With a clear focus on emerging technologies, intelligent systems, operational efficiency and responsible growth, your Company is well positioned to support enterprises in their digital evolution, both in India and globally.** 

##### **Dear Shareholders,** 

I am pleased to share with you the Integrated Annual Report for financial year 25–26. 

### A Company Built for What's Next 

We are focused on making businesses stronger by enabling seamless connectivity, securing critical operations, and advancing the technologies shaping the future. This remains the standard we bring to every client, across every market. 

This has been a year of purposeful progress: A year in which your Company not only delivered strong results but also deepened its strategic foundations, sharpened its focus on innovation, and demonstrated, once again, that resilience and ambition can thrive together. 

At the core of this is the Company’s digital fabric – an integrated architecture spanning network, cloud, security, and collaboration. It brings these capabilities together into a unified ecosystem that reduces complexity, optimises costs, and enables scalable growth. Built for current demands and designed to evolve, it is becoming a preferred platform for enterprises. With a clear focus on emerging technologies, intelligent systems, operational efficiency and responsible growth, your Company is well positioned to support enterprises in their digital evolution, both in India and globally. 

As the world around us grows more complex, shaped by rapid technological change, shifting geopolitical currents, and evolving enterprise needs, I am proud to report that your Company has remained firmly on course: clear in its direction, confident in its capabilities, and committed to creating enduring value for every one of its stakeholders. 

### Performance: Resilience in a Testing Environment 

Operating in an increasingly dynamic global environment, your Company delivered a consolidated revenue from operations of `H` 24,803 crore for FY 25–26. The performance was strengthened by the continued momentum of our data and digital portfolio. 

We are seeing a fundamental shift in how enterprises operate. Hybrid cloud, AI, IoT, edge computing and security are no longer emerging trends but core to business strategy. Among these, AI will be a defining force in the years ahead. 

The Board has accordingly proposed a dividend of `H` 17.50 per share for FY 25–26, subject to shareholder approval. This reflects your Company's financial discipline and its commitment to rewarding the trust you place in us. 

Your Company is approaching this shift with discipline, focusing not just on capability expansion, but on ensuring innovation is underpinned by governance, security, and accountability. 

During the year, your Company advanced its AI-ready portfolio with a clear strategic focus on helping enterprises adopt AI with confidence and clarity. Our platforms, built on our digital fabric are designed to simplify complexity, integrate capabilities and enable more intelligent operations across environments. 

Macroeconomic headwinds and geopolitical disruptions, including the continued uncertainty arising from the conflict in West Asia, have introduced caution into global IT spending. Yet, your Company has navigated these conditions with characteristic resilience, drawing on the depth of its capabilities and the enduring trust of its customers across all segments of its digital fabric. We remain confident in our ability to continue converting challenge into opportunity by demonstrating value to our customers. 

We also strengthened our position through targeted innovations and partnerships, including enhanced network capabilities, AI-led orchestration and collaboration with global technology leaders. These efforts are enabling enterprises to move more 

decisively from data and insights to real-time, intelligent action, while reinforcing trust and scalability in increasingly AI-driven ecosystems. 

### Trust as a Guiding Principle 

As digital systems become more deeply embedded within enterprise, the role of trust becomes paramount. 

For Tata Communications, trust of our customers and other stakeholders has always been foundational. Today, this extends across areas such as governance, cybersecurity, data protection and responsible technology deployment. 

In a world where expectations continue to evolve, our commitment to integrity and transparency remains a defining strength. It is through such consistency that enduring stakeholder confidence is built and sustained. 

This trust is reflected in an industry-leading Net Promoter Score of 83 (and 95 in the India market) a golden benchmark among our global peer group. These are not metrics to be reported and moved past. They represent the voice of our customers, and they affirm that your Company's growth strategy of migrating customers to higher value bands while maintaining uncompromising execution is working precisely as intended. 

### Sustainability: A Responsibility We Embrace 

Your Company continues to advance its commitment to sustainable and inclusive growth. In alignment with Project Aalingana, the Tata Group’s unified commitment towards Driving Net Zero, Pioneering Circular Economy and Preserving Nature & Biodiversity, your Company continues to make steady progress across climate action, resource stewardship and community resilience initiatives. 

Internally, your Company is taking decisive steps to reduce its environmental footprint. Our pledge to achieve Net Zero across global operations by 2035 is not an aspiration, it is an anchor for every decision we make. During the year, we continued to expand renewable energy adoption, improve energy efficiency and advance low-carbon transition initiatives, driving reductions in operational emissions intensity. We also strengthened our circularity and biodiversity efforts through achievement of Zero Waste to Landfill and biodiversity baseline assessment initiatives at our Pune campus for habitat improvement. 

Your Company also continued to deepen its commitment towards preserving nature and strengthening ecological resilience through water stewardship, biodiversity and community-led conservation initiatives. Programmes such as Vitalize Rural, Nanneer and Project Sahjeevan contributed towards water replenishment, habitat restoration and renewable energy access in vulnerable communities. These efforts were further strengthened through disaster risk reduction frameworks and targeted mental and social well-being interventions, reinforcing community resilience for the long term. 

### Leadership Transition 

The year marks an important change in leadership. 

On behalf of the Board, I would like to express our sincere appreciation and heartfelt gratitude to Mr. A.S. Lakshminarayanan who retired this year after over 7 years of extraordinary leadership as Managing Director and CEO. Under his stewardship, your Company achieved remarkable milestones, and his strategic clarity, personal integrity and deep dedication have left a lasting and positive impact on our organisation. 

It is with equal warmth that I welcome Mr. Ganesh Lakshminarayanan as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. He assumes leadership at a time of significant opportunity, supported by a strong foundation built over the years. 

I would also like to recognise the contributions of Mr. Kabir Ahmed Shakir, whose leadership as Chief Financial Officer has helped strengthen your Company’s financial discipline and resilience during a period of significant transformation. I am equally pleased to welcome Mr. Siddhartha Mundra as Chief Financial Officer. He brings strong experience and a clear perspective, as we continue to build on your Company’s financial and strategic priorities. 

The Board looks forward to the fresh energy that will be infused by Ganesh and Siddhartha’s leadership as we write the next chapter together. 

### Looking Ahead 

The path ahead presents both opportunities and challenges. 

The opportunity has never been greater. Demand for secure, scalable and intelligent digital capabilities is expected to continue growing, even as global uncertainties persist. 

Our path forward is guided by the same principles that have always defined us: relentless innovation, a genuine commitment to our customers, and the determination to build a sustainable future, for our business, our communities, and our planet. I remain deeply confident in our ability to create meaningful and lasting value for every stakeholder who places their trust in Tata Communications. 

Finally, I am deeply grateful to our shareholders, customers, partners and employees. Your continued support and belief in Tata Communications are what make all of this possible. The best, I am certain, is yet to come. 

The journey ahead will require both resolve and foresight— and I am certain that your Company will continue to rise to the occasion. 

In doing so, we remain guided by the enduring principle that business must create value not only for itself, but for the communities and stakeholders it serves—reinforcing trust, responsibility and purpose at every step. 

Warm regards, 

#### **N. Ganapathy Subramaniam** 

Chairman

### Reimagining the AI Era 

Our progress is best understood through the evolution of each layer of our digital fabric. **<u>23.7% 15.2%</u>** 

Next-Gen Connectivity Cloud and Security Fabric (part of Network Fabric) **<u>16.9% 12.8%</u>** Interaction Fabric Media and Entertainment (including IoT) portfolio 

**Network Fabric:** Our Network Fabric remains the backbone of our portfolio, evolving beyond high-performance connectivity into an intelligent, programmable and self-healing network. During FY 25-26, we expanded AI-enabled automation to enable real-time optimisation, faster fault resolution and improved service resilience for global enterprises. Networkled data revenues continue to anchor our performance. 

**Cloud Fabric:** Our Cloud and Security Fabric continues to enable enterprises to securely connect and manage increasingly distributed workloads across hybrid and multi cloud environments. Growth in our Digital Portfolio was driven by rising adoption of secure cloud networking, Secure Access Service Edge ('SASE')-aligned architectures and sovereign infrastructure. 

### Building AI ready foundations across the digital fabric 

Over the past year, we have taken deliberate and structured steps to embed AI across our own organisation. A key milestone in this journey has been the development of our AI Maturity Assessment Framework, which evaluates each business unit across capability and outcomes, and maps progress across defined maturity levels. This provides us with a clear view of our current position, highlights areas for focused intervention and ensures that our investments in AI remain disciplined, scalable and aligned to measurable outcomes. 

**Interaction Fabric:** Our Interaction Fabric has emerged as a key growth engine, strengthened by Kaleyra<sup>TM</sup> and further accelerated by the acquisition of Commotion. This has significantly enhanced our capabilities in AI-led customer engagement, spanning voice AI, automation, personalisation and real-time orchestration across channels. While still at an early stage, Commotion strengthens our ability to deliver outcome-led, AI-powered solutions and deepens our participation in the evolving enterprise AI ecosystem. 

This year, we advanced our AI-ready portfolio under a clear strategic intent: helping organisations adopt AI with confidence and clarity. Our newly launched suite, comprising Tata Communications IZO<sup>TM</sup> + Multi Cloud Network, Tata Communications Edge Distribution Platform, and ThreadSpan™, is built on our digital fabric to remove silos, simplify operations, and embed trust across the digital continuum. 

What is changing, however, is not just the strength of each fabric, but how they are converging into a single, AI embedded platform - the digital fabric operating as one. 

**ThreadSpan™:** We launched ThreadSpan™ as a key pillar of our AI-ready portfolio, designed to simplify the growing complexity of hybrid and multi cloud environments. By continuously discovering and correlating data across systems, it enables real-time decision-making, reduces operational complexity and strengthens resilience, providing enterprises with a single, integrated control plane to securely scale AIdriven and data-intensive workloads. 

We also unveiled IZO™ Data Centre Dynamic Connectivity: a software-defined solution that allows enterprises to dynamically and ‘on-demand’ connect their data centres to cloud providers, partners through high-performance private networks. 



**Our newly launched suite, comprising Tata Communications IZO**<sup>**TM**</sup> **+ Multi Cloud Network, Tata Communications Edge Distribution Platform, and ThreadSpan™, is built on our digital fabric to remove silos, simplify operations, and embed trust across the digital continuum.**

## Together, limitless<sup>TM</sup> 

This year, we introduced our new brand identity—Together, limitless<sup>TM</sup> . This is not merely a brand articulation; it reflects the essence of how Tata Communications is evolving. 

At its core, Together, limitless<sup>TM</sup> represents our belief that the greatest value is created when technology, platforms, ecosystems and partnerships come together seamlessly to deliver outcomes that go beyond conventional boundaries. It brings to life our transition from delivering individual solutions to enabling integrated, end-to-end digital experiences for our customers. 

For us, it signifies a more connected, collaborative and purpose-driven way of working, where we co-create with customers, leverage the strength of our digital fabric, and harness the power of AI and innovation to help enterprises scale, adapt and thrive in an increasingly complex world. 

## Trust, Responsibility and People: At the Heart of Transformation 

Our customers rely on us not only for performance, but for security, reliability and responsible innovation. At the heart of our transformation lies the trust we continue to build with our customers. This is reflected not only in consistent improvements in our Net Promoter Score of 83 (and 95 in the India market), but also in the depth and quality of 

our engagements across global enterprises. Our employee engagement score remains strong at 83%. This score is 6% higher than the Global Engagement Top Quartile benchmark, and we remain consistently positioned in the top quartile of engagement across diverse industries worldwide. 

Our recognition as a Leader in the Gartner<sup>®</sup> Magic Quadrant™ for Global WAN Services for the 13<sup>th</sup> consecutive year, alongside Frost & Sullivan’s 2025 Global Company of the Year Award for Video Managed Services, reinforces our ability to translate strategy into execution at scale. These recognitions validate the growing relevance of our platform-led digital fabric and our role as a trusted partner in enabling complex, AI-driven transformation journeys for our customers. 

As we scale our digital platforms and AI capabilities, responsibility remains central to how we grow. Our sustainability approach is anchored in the principles of People, Planet and Community, with strong Governance at its core, ensuring that business growth remains aligned with long-term environmental and social impact. During the year, we strengthened climate disclosures, advanced sustainable infrastructure practices and continued to enhance workplace safety and well-being frameworks across our operations. Tata Communications' recognition in the CDP Climate Leadership Band and successful achievement of Sustainability Linked Loan performance target reflect the strength of our climate action roadmap. We were also honoured with multiple recognitions across sustainability, CSR and safety, reaffirming our commitment to responsible and resilient growth. 

Importantly, our digital solutions continue to enable customers to improve their own sustainability outcomes through secure, scalable and energy-efficient technologies, while our AI platforms are being developed with strong governance, security and ethical frameworks to ensure innovation is scaled responsibly and with trust.

## Financial Performance in FY 25-26 

In FY 25-26, Data Revenue increased to `H` 21,352 crore from `H` 19,513 crore in FY 24-25, reflecting sustained growth in the Company’s digital portfolio and continued adoption of its digital fabric solutions. Profit After Tax ('PAT') declined to `H` 1,044 crore compared to `H` 1,625 crore in FY 25, with PAT margin moderating from 7.0% to 4.2%, primarily due to the impact of a non-recurring income from land monetisation recorded in the previous year. 

The underlying operating performance remained stable, with EBITDA margins largely sustained. Net debt to EBITDA improved further, closing below 2.0x in FY 25-26, supported by prudent capital allocation, strong operating cash flows and disciplined balance sheet management. 

#### **Strengthening Revenue Visibility and Quality** 

Over recent years, the enterprise order book has grown at a healthy pace, with the digital portfolio accounting for an increasing share. Digital platforms allow us to deepen our relationships with customers, increasing our relevance to them. This improves structured financial planning and visibility. 

International operations continue to play a critical role in strengthening scale, diversification and visibility. Investment decisions have been guided with a clear focus on profitability thresholds, operating leverage and working capital discipline, ensuring growth does not come at the expense of financial stability.

Our financial strategy is anchored in two parallel priorities: scaling digital platforms and maintaining capital efficiency. 

Investments were directed toward launching and scaling digital services across cloud, security, AI-led interaction and edge services. Many of these higher margin offerings were introduced towards the latter part of the year and are still in early stages of ramp-up. 

The acquisition of Commotion Inc., (‘Commotion’) during the year formed an integral part of the capital allocation strategy. The acquisition was undertaken to enhance our customer interaction and AI-led journey orchestration, enabling enterprises to design more predictive and outcome focused customer journeys. When combined with Kaleyra’s platforms, Commotion helps improve our go-to-market strategy across various use cases. The acquisition also builds on existing product investments, including Tata Communications Vayu Cloud, by enabling AI workloads to 

run in a governed and efficient manner, improving capital efficiency and expanding revenue opportunities across the enterprise customer base. The acquisition was assessed through a portfolio lens, balancing strategic relevance with expected returns and scalability over time. 

## Financial Resilience through Structured Planning 

Financial planning at Tata Communications incorporates structured scenario analysis and both long-range and shortrange planning cycles. In a year characterised by evolving macroeconomic conditions and heightened market volatility, maintaining financial resilience required planned strategic interventions. Through structured planning frameworks and robust cost governance, we continued to safeguard margins, preserve cash flows and sustain operating stability, while supporting ongoing investments in our digital capabilities. 

We have a comprehensive and disciplined approach to financial management by evaluating multiple operating scenarios and evolving market conditions to proactively anticipate change and enable timely strategic responses. This is supported by continuous performance monitoring that allows us to assess outcomes against market dynamics and recalibrate plans as needed. 

Performance across businesses is continuously evaluated using a common financial framework covering revenue growth, EBITDA margins, ROCE, leverage and free cash flows. This ensures that variation in volume growth or pricing dynamics across services does not compromise consolidated financial health. 

FY 25–26 has been a year of focused execution, balancing strategic investments with continued focus on capital efficiency and financial resilience. As we scaled our digital platforms across cloud, AI, security and interaction services, we remained committed to structured capital allocation guided by clear focus on long-term value creation. Our financial strategy remains anchored in delivering sustainable growth and cash flows with disciplined execution.

## Enhancing the shareholder experience 

Enhancing the experience of our shareholders in interactions with the Company remains an important focus area for us. Technology enabled platforms and responsive service models such as Investor Relations Contact Centres and a 24/7 AI-enabled Chatbot maintained by our Registrar and Transfer Agent are used to make interactions simpler, faster and more accessible. These efforts are aimed at improving ease of engagement, strengthening service delivery and ensuring timely resolution of shareholder queries. 

During the year, our efforts were aligned with regulatory initiatives led by SEBI and the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority, including the Saksham Niveshak campaign. This nationwide initiative focused on investor awareness, KYC and nomination updates, and facilitating the claim of unclaimed dividends. The initiative received encouraging participation and positive feedback from shareholders, reflecting improved awareness, timely compliance and stronger engagement. 

New engagement formats, including curated learning sessions and visits to our Customer Experience Centres, have further deepened investor understanding of emerging platforms and technologies. 

During the year, the Annual Investor Day saw participation from over 85 investors and analysts. Global outreach was expanded across key geographies, including India, Singapore, Hong Kong and the UAE, supporting a consistent two way exchange of insights and perspectives.

It enables seamless orchestration across heterogeneous networks, cloud platforms, interaction channels and connected assets, providing consistent performance, robust security and visibility. 

environments, allowing enterprises to transition from siloed operations to coordinated, intelligent decisionmaking. This integrated model reduces fragmentation, improves operational agility and enables customers to scale with confidence. 

Together, our platforms support enterprise transformation across customer interaction, workforce collaboration, industrial operations and digital media—delivered on a resilient and future-ready foundation.

# **190+** **<u>650+ countries</u>** 

Our Network Fabric provides the global infrastructure backbone for customer’s networks, a connectivity layer that underpins our digital fabric. Retail Banking Contact Centre Transformation 

##### **Business Challenge** 

A major retail banking organisation serving over 21 million customers was supported by an extensive agent network operating through fragmented legacy processes. This resulted in slow service cycles, high manual dependency, limited scalability and challenges in meeting evolving customer experience expectations while ensuring GDPR compliance. 

##### **Our Solution** 

We delivered a cloud-native Contact Centre as a Service (CCaaS) transformation, consolidating legacy processes into a unified omnichannel platform. The solution integrated AI capabilities such as Voice Bots, Agent Copilot, predictive analytics and automated workflows, along with a unified agent desktop to streamline operations. 

##### **Key Outcomes** 

The transformation improved operational efficiency and customer experience while reducing manual workload. It enabled faster response times, improved agent productivity and ensured secure, compliant operations.

### Unified Communications as a Service ('UCaaS'): Enabling Consistent Collaboration at a Global Scale 

While customer engagement and connected ecosystems build enterprise interaction, internal collaboration remains a critical enabler of productivity, resilience and experience delivery. Our Interaction Fabric supports large scale, global workforce collaboration through a managed, platform agnostic UCaaS model. 

Tata Communications' UCaaS enables enterprises to standardise voice and collaboration services across regions while navigating the complexity of multi platform adoption, regulatory diversity and rapid workforce scaling. Anchored in robust global voice infrastructure and end to end lifecycle management, these offerings support the full journey, from assessment and migration to provisioning, monitoring and ongoing optimisation. 

##### **Simplifying Collaboration Across Platforms and Geographies** 

We operate in increasingly multi-vendor collaboration environments, with enterprises adopting platforms such as Microsoft Teams, Webex Calling, Zoom Phone and Google Workspace. Through our UCaaS offerings, we bring these disparate ecosystems together under a single, managed framework, integrating cloud, voice, Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) services, numbering, devices and meeting room infrastructure. 

This vendor agnostic approach provides flexibility to evolve collaboration strategies without operational disruption. By combining global PSTN coverage with platform native models such as Operator Connect and Direct Routing, we significantly accelerate deployment timelines. Apart from reducing rollouts from months to weeks, it also ensures consistent performance and policy control across locations. 

##### **Resilient, Secure and Compliant by Design** 

We have built our UCaaS offerings on Tata Communications’ carrier grade global network, enabling high availability voice services at scale. Through centralised monitoring, proactive analytics and automated workflows, we strengthen reliability, improve visibility and accelerate issue resolution, particularly in high volume enterprise environments. 

In addition, security and compliance are embedded across the solution. Capabilities such as Fraud Protection as a Service ('FPaaS') provide real time anomaly detection and automated mitigation, while unified numbering governance ensures compliance with country specific regulations across markets. As a single global voice provider, we simplify operations by removing the complexity of managing multiple local carriers and regulatory frameworks.

Innovation at Tata Communications is purpose led and deeply embedded in how we build, scale and evolve our digital fabric to create sustainable value in a dynamic operating environment. As enterprises navigate rapid technological change, our innovation engine focuses on translating emerging ideas into market ready solutions that strengthen platforms, enhance customer outcomes and support sustainable growth. 

Our approach is guided by a simple belief: innovation must be **relevant, customer validated and commercially meaningful** . 

By combining horizon scanning, ecosystem collaboration and disciplined validation, we ensure that innovation efforts are closely aligned to customer priorities, market trajectories and enterprise value creation. 

In alignment to our vision and growth, we are investing in building AI-embedded capabilities and innovations across our portfolio, customer experience and operations. ##### **Project Nanneer by Tata Communications (Chennai):**

Floating garden at Nagan Thangal Lake, restored under Project Nanneer by Tata Communications 

##### **A Story of Change** 

## Project Nanneer by Tata Communications 



Launched in 2022, Project Nanneer by Tata Communications revitalised the Nagan Thangal Lake, transforming a degraded waterbody into a thriving ecological and community asset. The intervention tripled lake storage capacity, improved groundwater recharge and reduced surrounding barren land, while restoring local biodiversity. Today, the lake supports the revival of **14 Fish species, 56 Bird species and 33 Butterfly species** , strengthening water security, ecosystem health and community engagement. Nagan Thangal Lake, at full capacity, preserves **1,078 tCO2e (tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent)** . 

##### **Climate Resilient Villages (Meghalaya):**

# Health, Safety and Well-being 

## **Safety in Every Setting** 

Health and safety at Tata Communications is guided by three core pillars: **risk mitigation, employee well-being and technology-enabled governance.** Together, they ensure consistent standards across offices, field operations and remote work environments. 

At Tata Communications, the health, safety and well being of every employee is non negotiable. We adopt a zero tolerance approach to unsafe practices supported by structured governance, proactive interventions and increasing use of digital tools. 

Risk Mitigation and Hazard Control 

Beyond physical safety, employee well being is supported through initiatives addressing mental, emotional and social health. The Recharge Squad, an employee led volunteer network, drives community building and well-being initiatives across global locations, reinforcing a supportive and connected workplace. 

Structured Hazard Identification and Risk Assessments help identify risks early and embed controls into daily operations. High-risk activities are managed through Mandatory Safety Standards, a digital Permit-to-Work system and the e-Safety Passport, which validates training before critical tasks are assigned.

Safety Week at our offices<br><!-- End of picture text -->

### Employee Health and Well-being 

Safe and healthy workplaces are enabled through ergonomic assessments, indoor air quality checks, fire readiness and safety inductions. Mental health programmes, wellness initiatives and awareness sessions further support employee well-being. 

### Technology-enabled Governance 

Digital tools strengthen transparency and accountability across the safety ecosystem. Online permit to work, mobile hazard reporting, digital audits and competency tracking help improve traceability, response and governance across work environments.

Addressing climate change remains a key priority for Tata Communications. Our climate strategy is anchored in a clear decarbonisation pathway, with an aim to achieve Carbon neutrality by 2030 and Net-Zero emissions (Scope 1, 2 and 3) by 2035. 

### Energy Efficiency and Renewable Transition 

Improving how we consume energy is central to reducing our environmental footprint. Ongoing energy efficiency projects across our offices and network facilities have delivered measurable reductions in consumption and costs. 

Progress is guided by global frameworks, including the GHG Protocol and Science Based Targets initiative, and strengthened through scenario-based climate risk assessments. 

At the same time, we continue to expand adoption of renewable energy through a mix of rooftop solar, group captive arrangements and green tariffs, guided by feasibility, long term value and site readiness. Improvements in Power Usage Effectiveness of network centres reflect a sustained focus on operational excellence alongside sustainability.

Energy-Efficient Infrastructure 

Intelligent hardware that adjusts power consumption dynamically, entering lowenergy modes during off-peak periods. 



Centralised, remote management that reduces on-site interventions and associated travel emissions. 

Cloud-First Operations 



Hardware Elimination 

Virtualising network functions to minimise equipment lifecycle impact. 



Real-Time Advanced monitoring tools Energy Insights to optimise energy use and continuously improve performance.

# Community-based Offsets and Local Impact 

Our community-based carbon offset programmes support our carbon neutrality goals while also creating meaningful benefits for local communities. 

Agroforestry initiatives help generate livelihoods, while improved cookstove projects reduce indoor air pollution and improve household health. These initiatives have been registered under Verra’s Verified Carbon Standard and also generate verified carbon credits, which help offset greenhouse gas emissions. 

By reducing dependence on traditional biomass, these programmes contribute to cleaner air and healthier living conditions. The carbon credits generated are fully traceable and aligned with recognised global standards. 

We select and scale these nature-based, community-led initiatives based on local needs, with ongoing monitoring to ensure they deliver both environmental and social impact. 

# Water Stewardship and Resource Conservation 

Responsible water management remains a priority, particularly in water stressed locations. Site level monitoring, IoT enabled tracking and preventive maintenance help us improve visibility and reduce consumption. Increased use of recycled water and rainwater harvesting contributes to improved water efficiency and reduced dependence on freshwater sources. 

Investments in rainwater harvesting, recycling systems and watershed development enhance resource efficiency while contributing to long-term water security. Our push towards water neutrality combines operational efficiency with community based replenishment initiatives, supporting long term water security for both our operations and surrounding communities.

#### **Embedding Ethics into Everyday Decisions** 

Continuous learning remains central to reinforcing governance expectations. Through structured training, leadership engagement and proactive communication, we ensure that ethical conduct, compliance and accountability remain integral to everyday decision-making. 

Ethical conduct is at the core of how we operate. Extending beyond policies, it is integral to our organisational culture and guides our day to day decisions and behaviours. 

The **Tata Code of Conduct** encapsulates our ethical obligations and responsibilities for committing towards a better tomorrow for the community, society and the world at large. All employees are required to complete annual mandatory e-learning trainings on the Tata Code of Conduct, with assessments embedded to reinforce understanding. New employees complete this training as part of onboarding, while targeted sessions conducted by the Legal Compliance team support consistent interpretation across functions.

##### **Information Security and Data Privacy: Enabling Digital Trust** 

As a global digital infrastructure provider, trust is fundamental to our business. Information security and data privacy are therefore embedded as core pillars of our governance framework. 

##### **Privacy by Design** 

We have embedded privacy-by-design principles across our products, services, and processes. Each initiative undergoes structured privacy impact assessments to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements and the safeguarding of personal data. 

Our key capabilities include: 

Clearly defined processes for managing data subject rights, ensuring transparency and regulatory compliance 

Comprehensive data lifecycle management, spanning data collection, storage, usage, and secure disposal 

Deployment of privacy controls supported by periodic reporting to Management and the Board, enabling proactive oversight and accountability 

##### **Robust Cybersecurity Framework** 

We continue to maintain our ISO 27001:2022 certification, reflecting adherence to globally recognised information security standards. Our cybersecurity strategy is aligned with business priorities and built on the following principles: 



Proactive identification and effective management of security and privacy risks 

Design and implementation of security controls with minimal disruption to customer experience 

Continuous innovation to address evolving business and threat landscapes 

Adoption of a “shift-left” approach, leveraging automation and fail-safe defaults to enhance resilience 

##### **Strengthening Digital Trust through Governance** 

As we advance our network and platform services, we continue to strengthen our security and data privacy posture by managing emerging risks, enhancing cyber resilience, and maintaining a secure and trusted technology environment. This is supported by continuous improvement in preventive and detective controls, robust governance, and the adoption of advanced technologies such as AI-driven security, cloud security, and breach and attack simulation. We have also implemented comprehensive metrics and scorecards across business platforms, enabling regular review by senior leadership and the Board. 

Together, these measures ensure our Information Security and Data Privacy programme remains aligned with our growth strategy, driving resilience, safeguarding stakeholder interests, and reinforcing long-term digital trust. 

##### **Embedding ESG into Governance** 

Governance at Tata Communications integrates ESG priorities into enterprise decision-making. 

- y Board-level oversight through the CSR, Safety and Sustainability Committee 

- y ESG metrics integrated into the Corporate Scorecard 

- y Transparent disclosures aligned with global frameworks, including GRI, and supported by third-party assurance

# **Navigating Risk with Confidence** 

At Tata Communications, our risk management approach is anchored in a structured, forward-looking framework that adapts to an increasingly dynamic environment. Operating across diverse geographies, we continuously track external developments to stay prepared for potential disruptions and ensure business continuity. This approach enables us to remain resilient and deliver consistently on our commitments. By embedding risk into strategic and operational decisionmaking, supported by a strong governance framework, we reinforce agility and stability in executing our growth strategy.

### **Cybersecurity and Data Privacy** 

#### **Cyber Attacks and Data Privacy Breach** 

## Risk Integration and Monitoring 

Risk insights are embedded into our strategic and operational decision-making, ensuring that business priorities are aligned with a clear understanding of exposures and mitigation actions. Continuous capability-building initiatives, including focused risk champion programmes, foster a strong riskaware culture and enhance responsiveness across functions. Structured surveillance mechanisms, through quarterly and event-driven reviews with business risk owners, provide ongoing visibility into risk exposure, severity and mitigation progress. 

In addition, continuous tracking of key geopolitical and macroeconomic developments enables early identification of potential disruptions and supports timely responses, strengthening organisational resilience and continuity. 

During the year, early-warning indicators were also reviewed across key geopolitical and macroeconomic developments, including potential tariff changes in the United States and Mexico, Indo-Pak tensions, China’s rare earth export controls, instability in the Middle East and the Red Sea cable cut incident.

**Mr. N. Ganapathy Subramaniam** Chairman and Non-Executive Director 

Mr. N. Ganapathy Subramaniam was the Chief Operating Officer (‘COO’) and Executive Director of Tata Consultancy Services Limited (‘TCS’) from February 2017 till May 2024. He joined the Board of Tata Communications on December 2, 2021 and became the Chairman on March 14, 2025. He is also a Director and Chairman of Tata Elxsi Limited and Tejas Networks Limited. He has over 40 years of experience in TCS in strategic management of technology and operations, across large corporations in both established and new growth markets. He has played a strategic role in several landmark initiatives that TCS undertook across banking, telecom and public services globally. He has also been part of the evolution of Indian IT industry, and the value creation process with a globally distributed talent. He has in depth knowledge of technology, operations, product development, business transformation and change management as organisations manage their technology and business. 



# **Mr. Ashok Sinha** Independent Director 

Mr. Ashok Sinha is Chairman, 4 I Advisors, a proprietary consulting firm that provides a specialised spectrum of technical consultancy and advisory services in the area of Energy, Technology and Finance since December 2010. He has a wealth of experience, competencies, and expertise from his leadership journey as the Chairman and Managing Director of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (‘BPCL’). He spent 33 years in BPCL, where he served on the Board of BPCL for 15 years – first as Director (Finance) for 10 years and then as its Chairman and Managing Director for 5 years. He has been conferred with the India Chief Financial Officer Award 2001 for Information and Knowledge Management by the Economic Intelligence Unit (‘EIU’) India and American Express. He is also the recipient of the CIO-100 Award (USA)- 1999 for the top 100 firms worldwide for their innovative practices that leverage people and technology. Since 2011, he has served as an Independent Director in companies in diverse industries. Mr. Ashok Sinha joined the Board of Tata Communications as an Independent Director on October 8, 2021. 



# **Mr. Krishnakumar Natarajan** Independent Director 

A leading authority in the global IT sector, Mr. Krishnakumar Natarajan co-founded Mindtree in 1999 and has played key roles in building the company’s innovative approach to delivering IT services and solutions to global 2000 enterprises. He is a 40-year IT industry veteran and also serves as an advisor of Nasscom Foundation. He is a regular speaker at international IT industry conferences and a faculty member at management schools around the world. Social enterprises and philanthropy are some of his other key interests. Along with his wife Akila he runs their personal foundation “Mela” which is focused on helping high potential rural girls to attain professional qualifications and helping senior citizens age gracefully. Mr. Krishnakumar joined the Board of Tata Communications as Independent Director on July 15, 2021. 



**Mr. Ankur Verma** Non-Executive Director 

Mr. Ankur Verma, a B.E. in Mechanical Engineering and PGDM from IIM, Calcutta has around 25 years of experience in Investment Banking, Capital Markets and Corporate Strategy. At present, Mr. Verma is Group Chief Strategy Officer at Tata Sons Private Limited, where he has responsibilities in strategy, corporate finance and mergers and acquisitions. Previously, he was Managing Director (Investment Banking Division) in Bank of America Merrill Lynch, and also Group Manager & Head, Business Planning in Infosys Technologies Limited – Corporate Planning Group. He currently serves on the boards of several Tata group companies. Mr. Verma joined the Board of Tata Communications as Non-Executive Director on April 19, 2023. 





# **Mr. Sujit Kumar Varma** Independent Director 

**Ms. Sangeeta Anand** Independent Director 

Mr. Sujit Kumar Varma is a career banker with proven track record of leading diverse business departments. Mr. Varma had been associated with the State Bank of India ('SBI') for over 30 years where he held several important positions viz., CEO - SBI New York USA, General Manager - Mid-Corporate Regional Office, Mumbai, India and Chief General Manager - International Banking. Mr. Varma superannuated as Deputy Managing Director, Corporate Accounts Group from SBI in January 2021. He is highly experienced in Corporate and Retail Credit, Trade Finance, International Banking, Risk Management and Compliance. Currently he is a director on the board of companies in diverse industries. Mr. Varma joined the Board of Tata Communications as an Independent Director on April 22, 2025. 

Sangeeta Anand is an independent public and private company board director and C-level technology executive with over 25 years of expertise in AI, cybersecurity, cloud, and enterprise software. She has served as an Independent Director of Tata Communications Limited since September 5, 2024 and is a member of its Risk Management Committee. 

Ms. Anand previously served for five years as an Independent Director of The Sage Group PLC (LON: SGE), a FTSE 100 company, where she was a member of the Audit and Risk Committee. Her executive career includes roles as SVP of Product Management and Marketing at F5 Inc., General Manager at SafeNet Inc. (acquired by Thales Group), CMO at Alkira, and two VP roles during her 12 years at Cisco Systems. She began her career at Oracle Corporation. 

Ms. Anand holds MBAs from The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, and Symbiosis Institute of Business Management, Pune, and has completed executive education in AI at UC Berkeley and a Board Director program at Harvard Business School. 





**Mr. Ganesh Lakshminarayanan** Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer 

**Mr. P. Jagdish Rao** Independent Director 

Mr. P. Jagdish Rao is a seasoned banking, financial services and technology executive with over 35 years of experience at Citibank and Citigroup, where he played a pivotal role in driving large scale business transformations, optimising global banking operations, and implementing advanced technology platforms. He has deep expertise in cybersecurity, data analytics and corporate governance, having interacted extensively with the Citigroup Board for 20 years. Throughout his career, Mr. Rao has held various senior leadership positions, including Chairman of Citigroup Technology Inc., Chief Administrative Officer for the Global Consumer Bank and twice serving as Citigroup’s Chief Information Security Officer. He has extensive experience in mergers and acquisitions, divesting several Citi subsidiaries globally and managing corporate operations across diverse regions such as Asia, Europe, Latin America and the US. Mr. Rao joined the Board of Tata Communications as an Independent Director on June 13, 2025. 

Mr. Ganesh Lakshminarayanan has more than 30 years of international management experience, working with multinational corporations, B2B startups, and Indian enterprises. As the MD, Group Vice President for ServiceNow - India and SAARC, he was responsible for driving market growth for ServiceNow. Before joining ServiceNow, he was the CEO of Airtel Business in India and prior to that the CEO of Airtel's Enterprise Business unit. Academically, Ganesh has earned an MBA with high distinction from the Ross School of Business at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor. Additionally, he holds a BS in Computer Science and Engineering, graduating as a gold medalist from Guindy Engineering College in Chennai, India. Ganesh has been elected twice to the NASSCOM executive council and served on the FICCI council. Additionally, he is a founding member of Social Venture Partners Bengaluru. He was appointed as the Managing Director & CEO by the Board of Tata Communications on May 20, 2026.

## **10. Book Closure, Record Date and Dividend:** 

The Board of Directors at its meeting held on April 22, 2026 has recommended a final dividend of `H` 17.50/- per equity share of `H` 10/- each (i.e., 175%). The Company has fixed Friday, June 19, 2026 as the ‘Record Date’ for determining entitlement of Members to final dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, if approved at the AGM. The Register of Members and the Share Transfer Books of the Company will be closed from Saturday, June 20, 2026 till Tuesday, June 23, 2026, both days inclusive. Final dividend, if approved at the AGM, will be paid subject to tax deduction at source on or after Friday, July 10, 2026 as under: 

- a. to all Beneficial Owners in respect of shares held in electronic form as per the data made available by the NSDL and Central Depository Services (India) Limited (‘CDSL’) as of close of business hours on Friday, June 19, 2026; and 

- b. to all Members in respect of shares held in physical form whose names appear on the Company’s Register of Members after giving effect to all valid transmission or transposition requests lodged with the Company or the RTA as of close of business hours on Friday, June 19, 2026. 

## **11. Mandatory Electronic Payment of Dividend** 

SEBI, vide its circular dated November 17, 2023 read with SEBI Master Circular dated February 6, 2026, has mandated that dividend to shareholders holding shares in physical form shall be paid only through electronic mode. Such payment shall be made only if the folio is KYC compliant i.e., Permanent Account Number (‘PAN’), contact information, mobile number, complete bank details and specimen signatures are registered. In case of non-updation of any of these details in respect of physical folios, dividend shall be paid only upon furnishing of all the aforesaid details in entirety. 

In order to receive the dividend in a timely manner, Members holding shares in physical form should be KYC compliant. Members who have not submitted their KYC documents are requested to send these documents latest by Friday, June 19, 2026 to the RTA.

# **12. Tax deducted at Source (‘TDS’) on Dividend** 

Pursuant to the Income Tax Act, 2025 (‘IT Act’), dividend income is taxable in the hands of the Members and the Company is required to deduct TDS from dividend paid to the Members at rates prescribed in the IT Act including any amendments or modifications thereto. In general, to enable compliance with TDS requirements, Members are requested to complete and / or update their Residential Status, valid PAN linked to Aadhar, Category as per the IT Act with their DPs or in case shares are held in physical form, with the Company / RTA by sending the documents by Saturday, June 20, 2026 to enable the Company to determine the appropriate TDS / withholding tax rate applicable, verify the documents and provide exemption, as needed.

# **17.  Dematerialisation of Shares** 

As per Regulation 40 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, as amended, securities of listed companies can be transferred, transmitted and transposed only in dematerialised form. In view of this and to eliminate all risks associated with physical shares and for ease of portfolio management, Members holding shares in physical form are requested to consider converting their holdings to dematerialised form. Members can contact the RTA at <u>investor.helpdesk@ in.mpms.mufg.com</u> for assistance in this regard. 

Attention of Members is also drawn to the SEBI circular dated January 25, 2022 mandating all listed entities to issue securities in dematerialised form only while 

processing service requests relating to issue of duplicate securities certificate, claim from unclaimed suspense account renewal / exchange of securities certificate, endorsement, sub-division / splitting of securities certificate, consolidation of securities certificates / folios, transposition and transmission. Accordingly, Members are requested to submit duly filled Form ISR-4 or Form ISR-5, as applicable, for the above-mentioned requests and surrender their original securities certificate(s) for processing of service requests to the RTA. 

With effect from April 2, 2026, SEBI has dispensed with the requirement of issuance of a Letter of Confirmation by the Company / RTA while processing service requests. Accordingly, securities will be credited directly to the Member’s demat account upon submission of valid demat account details along with the latest Client Master List.

- **A. Voting through Electronic Means** 

   - i. Pursuant to the provisions of Section 108 of the Act read with Rule 20 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014, and Regulation 44 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, as amended, read with applicable SEBI and MCA Circulars, the Members are provided with the facility to cast their vote electronically, through the e-voting services provided by NSDL, on all the resolutions set forth in this Notice. 

   - ii. **The remote e-Voting period commences on Sunday, July 5, 2026 (9:00 a.m. IST) and ends on Wednesday, July 8, 2026 (5:00 p.m. IST).** During this period, Members holding shares either in physical form or in electronic form as on **Thursday, July 2, 2026 i.e., cut-off date,** may cast their vote electronically. The remote e-Voting module shall be disabled by NSDL for voting thereafter. Once the vote on 

a resolution is cast by a Member, the Member shall not be allowed to change it subsequently or cast vote again. 

- iii. Members have the option to cast their vote on any of the resolutions using the remote e-voting facility, either during the aforesaid period or e-voting facility during the AGM. Members attending the AGM through VC / OAVM, who have not cast their vote through remote e-Voting and are otherwise not barred from doing so, shall be eligible to vote through the e-Voting system during the AGM. Members who have cast their vote through remote e-Voting prior to the AGM may participate at the AGM but shall not be entitled to cast their vote again on the resolutions for which they have already cast their vote.

#### **General Guidelines for Shareholders** 

1. It is strongly recommended not to share your password with any other person and to take utmost care to keep your password confidential. 2. In case of any queries related to e-voting, you may refer the Frequently Asked Questions (‘FAQs’) for shareholders and e-Voting user manual for shareholders available at the download section of <u>www.evoting.nsdl.com.</u> For any grievances connected with facility for e-voting, please contact Mr. Sagar S. Gudhate, Assistant Vice President - NSDL at E-mail: <u>evoting@nsdl.com, phone: +91 22 4886 7000.</u> 

3. Members may send a request to <u>evoting@nsdl.com</u> for procuring User ID and password for e-voting by providing demat account number/folio number, client master or copy of consolidated account statement, PAN (self-attested scanned copy of PAN card), Aadhaar (self-attested scanned copy of Aadhaar card). 

4. The instructions for Members for e-voting on the day of the AGM are mentioned in Note No. 22 A. 

#### **B. Instructions for Members for attending the AGM through VC/OAVM** 

1. Members will be able to attend the AGM through VC/OAVM provided by NSDL at <u>https://www. evoting.nsdl.com</u> following the steps mentioned above for login to NSDL e-voting system. After successful login, you can see VC/OAVM link placed under “Join Meeting” menu against the Company name. You are requested to click on VC/ OAVM link placed under “Join Meeting” menu. 

Members who do not have the User ID and Password for e-voting or have forgotten the User ID and Password may retrieve the same by following the remote e-voting instructions mentioned in this Notice. Further Members can also use the OTP based login for logging into the e-voting system of NSDL. 

2. Facility of joining the AGM through VC/ OAVM shall open 30 minutes before the time scheduled for the AGM. 

3. Members who need assistance before or during the AGM may contact Mr. Sagar Gudhate, Assistant Vice President at <u>evoting@nsdl.com</u> or call on +91 22 4886 7000. 

**4. Registration as speaker shareholder** 

Members who would like to express their views or ask questions during the AGM may register themselves as a speaker by sending a request from their registered e-mail address mentioning their name, DP ID and Client ID / folio number, PAN and mobile number at <u>investor.relations@ tatacommunications.com</u> between **Friday, June 26, 2026 (9:00 a.m. IST) and Friday, July 3, 2026 (5:00 p.m. IST)** . The Company reserves the right to restrict the number of speakers depending on the availability of time for the AGM.

1. The Scrutinizer shall, immediately after the conclusion of voting at the Meeting, unblock the votes cast through e-Voting (votes cast during the AGM and vote cast through remote e-Voting) and make, not later than two working days from the conclusion of the AGM, a consolidated Scrutinizer’s Report of the total votes cast in favour or against, if any, to the Chairperson or a person authorised by the Chairperson in writing, who shall countersign the same. 

2. The results declared along with the Scrutinizer’s Report shall be placed on the Company’s website <u>www.tatacommunications.com</u> and on the website of NSDL <u>www.evoting.nsdl.com</u> immediately after declaration. The Company shall simultaneously forward the results to BSE and NSE, where the shares of the Company are listed. The results shall also be placed on the notice board of the Company at its Registered Office and Corporate Office.

# **Explanatory Statement** 

**Pursuant to Section 102(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’) the following Explanatory Statement sets out material facts relating to business mentioned under Item Nos. 5 and 6 of the accompanying Notice.** 

Vide letter dated May 19, 2026, the Company received approval from MIB for appointment of Mr. Lakshminarayanan as MD & CEO. The Company has also received the necessary consent and declarations from Mr. Lakshminarayanan confirming his eligibility to be appointed as the MD & CEO. 

## **In respect of Item No. 5** 

The NRC, at its meeting held on May 20, 2026, in terms of Section 161 of the Act and applicable rules thereunder, recommended appointment of Mr. Lakshminarayanan as an Additional Director and as the MD & CEO of the Company. 

Under the provisions of Section 148 of the Act read with the Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014, as amended, the Company is required to have its cost records audited by a Cost Accountant. In accordance with the provisions of Section 148 of the Act read with the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, the remuneration payable to the Cost Auditor is required to be ratified by the Members of the Company. 

Based on the aforementioned recommendation and approvals, the Board of Directors at its meeting held on May 20, 2026 approved the appointment of Mr. Ganapathi S. Lakshminarayanan (DIN: 01828104) as an Additional Director and as MD & CEO of the Company, to hold office for a term of five consecutive years with effect from May 20, 2026 up to May 19, 2031 (both days inclusive), subject to approval of the Members and other applicable regulatory approval from the Government of India and all other statutory authorities, if any. 

The Board, on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, has approved the appointment and remuneration of Ms. Ketki D. Visariya, Cost Accountant, as Cost Auditor to conduct the audit of the cost records of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2027 at a remuneration of `H` 6.60 lakhs plus applicable taxes and out of pocket expenses on actual basis capped at 3% of the remuneration. 

The Company has received notice under section 160 of the Act proposing his candidature as Director of the Company. If appointed, Mr. Lakshminarayanan will act as MD & CEO, not liable to retire by rotation. 

Accordingly, consent of the Members is sought by way of an Ordinary Resolution as set out at Item No. 5 of the accompanying Notice for ratification of the remuneration payable to the Cost Auditor for the financial year ending March 31, 2027. 

Key terms and conditions of appointment, including remuneration, forming part of the agreement with Mr. Lakshminarayanan for his appointment as MD & CEO are given  below and the same may also be read and treated as disclosure in compliance with the requirements of the Act: 

The Board recommends the Ordinary Resolution set out at Item No. 5 of the Notice for approval by the Members. 

None of the Directors and Key Managerial Personnel (‘KMP’) or their respective relatives are concerned or interested in the Resolution at Item No. 5 of the accompanying Notice.

# **B. Duties & Powers:** 

The MD & CEO shall devote his whole time and attention to the business of the Company and perform such duties as may be entrusted to him by the Board from time to time and separately communicated to him and exercise such powers as may be assigned to him, subject to the superintendence, control and directions of the Board in connection with and in the best interests of the business of the Company and the business of one or more of its associated companies and / or subsidiaries, including performing duties as assigned to the MD & CEO from time to time by serving on the boards of such associated companies and / or subsidiaries or any other executive body or any committee of such a company. 

# **C. Proposed Remuneration** 

Annual Fixed Compensation of `H` 4,00,00,000 (Rupees Four Crore) per annum. The Fixed Compensation will comprise of following components: 

- **a. Basic Salary:** `H` 11,66,667 (Rupees Eleven Lakh Sixty Six Thousand Six Hundred and Sixty Seven) per month - which is computed at 35% of Annual Fixed Compensation - with effect from the date of joining. Effective 2027, the annual increment payable will be due on 1<sup>st</sup> April each year and will be determined by the Board of Directors on the recommendation of the NRC, which will take into account the performance of the MD & CEO, the size of operations, performance of the Company and its subsidiaries/associates and other relevant factors. 

- **b. Benefits, Perquisites, Allowances:** 

   - Rent-free residential accommodation (furnished or otherwise) with the Company bearing the cost of repairs, maintenance, society charges and utilities (e.g., gas, electricity and water charges) for Company provided accommodation. 

## OR 

House Rent Allowance in lieu (in case residential accommodation is not provided by the Company). 

- Other perquisites and allowances with an option to choose from the components given below, subject to it being within the limits of the Annual Fixed Compensation: 

   - Children’s Education & Hostel Expense; 

   - Leave Travel Assistance; 

Special Allowance (SA): Any amount lying unallocated from the flexible allowance after distribution across the components specified above will be paid as Special Allowance. 

- Company-provided car as per the Company’s Policy. 

- Statutory Contributions to Provident Fund and Gratuity Fund as per the rules of the Company. For avoidance of doubt, it is clarified that notwithstanding anything contained in rules, the Company will not be required to make any contributions towards Superannuation Fund or Annuity Fund or any other retirement benefits. 

- Hospitalisation, Telecommunication and other benefits as per Company’s policy. 

It is clarified that the details mentioned under Hospitalisation, Telecommunication and other benefits shall not be included in computation of Annual Fixed Compensation. 

The compensation structure set out is subject to revision to the extent required to comply with any amendment, notification, guideline, or directive issued under applicable laws or regulations by any competent authority. The Company reserves the right to modify the compensation structure solely to ensure continued statutory and regulatory compliance. Any such modification may result in changes to net take-home compensation and related tax implications. 

- **c. Incentive Remuneration in the form of:** 

   - **Performance Linked Bonus:** A target of `H` 4,00,00,000 (Rupees Four Crore) will be delivered annually as performance bonus on the achievement of the Annual Operating Plan of the Company and specific Key Performance Indicators for the MD & CEO’s personal contributions. These parameters will be agreed with the MD & CEO, before the start of each financial year of the Company and finalised by the Board of the Company. 

   - **Long term incentive and employee stock units (‘RSUs’):** The target incentive under the Long term Incentive Plan (‘LTIP’ / ‘Plan’) in 2027 (covering FY 2027-28, FY 2028-29 and FY 2029-30) is intended to be `H` 7,50,00,000 (Rupees Seven Crore 

Fifty Lakhs). These incentives would be vested subject to the achievement of certain corporate performance criteria and such other parameters as may be considered appropriate from time to time by the Board / NRC. The target incentive under the LTIP / RSU Plan is subject to the overall ceilings stipulated in Section 197 of the Act and related rules. All unvested RSUs as on date of retirement shall remain outstanding and shall be eligible to vest on the vesting date based on actual achievement of the performance based vesting criteria prorated for the duration of employment until the date of retirement. 

For the period from date of joining and up to March 31, 2027, the amount of Performance Linked Bonus and Long-Term Incentive will be pro-rated for the actual period worked. 

- **d. One-time Cash Compensation in the form of:** 

   - `H` 2,00,00,000 (Rupees Two Crore) to be paid on completion of 6 months with the Company. 

   - `H` 2,00,00,000 (Rupees Two Crore) on completion of 1 year with the Company. 

   - `H` 2,50,00,000 (Rupees Two Crore Fifty Lakh) on completion of 2 years with the Company. 

   - `H` 2,50,00,000 (Rupees Two Crore Fifty Lakh) on completion of 3 years with the Company. 

In the event the MD & CEO voluntarily gives a notice of termination of the agreement within 12 months of receiving the respective amounts in point (d) above, the MD & CEO will have to pay the respective amounts paid to him (pre-tax) back to the Company. 

- **e. Minimum Remuneration:** Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein contained, where, in any financial year during the currency of the tenure of the MD & CEO, the Company has no profits or its profits are inadequate, the Company will pay the MD & CEO remuneration by way of salary, benefits, perquisites and allowances, bonus / performance linked incentive, long term incentive plan and / or commission as approved by the Board and shareholders, as applicable. 

      - **f. Insurance:** The Company shall keep and maintain the following insurance policies as per Company’s rules and policy: 

         - i. Directors and Officers Liability Insurance Policies; 

         - ii. Accident Insurance Policy; iii. Life Insurance Policy. 

- **D. Other Terms of Appointment:** 

   1. Variation: 

The terms and conditions of the appointment of the MD & CEO and / or the agreement may be altered and varied from time to time by the Board as it may, in its discretion deem fit, irrespective of the limits stipulated under Schedule V to the Act or any amendments made hereafter in this regard in such manner as may be agreed to between the Board and the MD & CEO, subject to such approvals as may be required. 

2. Selling Agency: 

   - The MD & CEO, so long as he functions as such, undertakes not to become interested or otherwise concerned, directly or through his spouse and / or children, in any selling agency of the Company. 

3. Tata Code of Conduct: 

   - The provisions of the Tata Code of Conduct shall be deemed to have been incorporated into the agreement by reference. The MD & CEO shall during his term, abide by the provisions of the Tata Code of Conduct in spirit and in letter and commit to assure its implementation. 

4. Personnel Policies: All personnel policies of the Company and the related rules which are applicable to other employees of the Company shall also be applicable to the MD & CEO, unless specifically provided otherwise.

<u>Brief profile of Mr. Ganapathi S. Lakshminarayanan is given below:</u> 

Mr. Ganapathi S. Lakshminarayanan (‘Ganesh’) has more than 30 years of international management experience, working with multinational corporations, B2B startups, and Indian enterprises. As the MD, Group Vice President for ServiceNow - India and SAARC, he was responsible for driving market growth for ServiceNow. Before joining ServiceNow, Ganesh was the CEO of Airtel Business in India and prior to that the CEO of Airtel’s Enterprise Business unit. Academically, Ganesh has earned an MBA with high distinction from the Ross School of Business at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor. Additionally, he holds a BS in Computer Science and Engineering, graduating as a gold medalist from Guindy Engineering College in Chennai, India. 

Ganesh has been elected twice to the NASSCOM executive council and served on the FICCI council. Additionally, he is a founding member of Social Venture Partners Bengaluru.

The consolidated performance of the Company and its subsidiaries has been referred to wherever required.
